notes.brief_deviation_spread: Brief formula matte' = min(1, matte / (1 - spread)) is NOT implemented: applied to the matte before the blur it is the identity for a binary layer alpha (so spread would do nothing), and applied after the blur it is a different model. Implemented instead the structure of Krita libs/image/layerstyles/kis_ls_drop_shadow_filter.cpp (read as a behaviour reference only, GPL, no code copied): spread_px = spread * size is grown as a hard disc dilation (Krita: Gaussian of spread_size then hard edge), blur_px = size - spread_px by Gaussian, then offset, then knockout. Spread 1 = hard matte grown by the full size; spread has no effect at size 0 (matches the Adobe community thread 'spread not working ... only shadows with hard edges'). Lead may reverse; only effect_math::reference_matte (DropShadow arm) and shadow_split change. Hand tests: tests/effects.rs drop_shadow_offset_blur_taps_and_spread.
notes.brief_acceptance_note_stroke: Acceptance 4 says the 8-neighbour ring is coverage 1 at distance 1. Under the Euclidean model the 12 edge-adjacent ring pixels are exactly 1 and the 4 corner pixels are 1.5 - sqrt(.5) = 0.79289 (round corners), 0 at distance >= 2; inside gives the 8-pixel inner ring exactly. Photoshop's outside-stroke corner shape is UNVERIFIED (D5 13).

memory_bound.model: bytes = 4 * floats of the live buffers, exact (receipt.peak_bytes == window_cost.peak_bytes, asserted for 14 ops x 3 windows; layer_window_cost asserted for the composed stack). For a window ww x wh, blur half-width kb, dilation radius kd: dilate stage (a0 + a1) * 4 + (kd + 1) * 4 with a0 = (ww + 2kb + 2kd)(wh + 2kb + 2kd), a1 = (ww + 2kb)(wh + 2kb); blur stage (a1 + ww * (wh + 2kb)) * 4, then (ww * (wh + 2kb) + ww * wh) * 4 + 8 * ww; post step 8 * ww * wh. Strokes: (a0 + ww * wh) * 4 + (kd + 1) * 4 per half (+ 4 * ww * wh for the centre). Composition adds 20 bytes per window pixel (result plane 16 + content alpha 4) to the largest single matte
memory_bound.examples: 64 x 64 window, drop shadow size 24 spread 0.5: about 99 KiB; one-pixel window, blur size 1000 (kb 1500): about 36 MB measured <= 64 MiB cap in the test
memory_bound.admission: WindowLimits{max_bytes, max_work}; the prediction is checked before the accessor is called or anything is allocated, every allocation is also charged against the running aggregate (unit test running_aggregate_is_charged_per_allocation), work = inner-loop visits (dilation (2kd + 1)^2 per output sample is an upper bound)

design_decisions: domain is an explicit geometry field because the reference truncates every intermediate at its plane edge; without it identity on planes whose alpha touches the edge would be impossible, with it uncut and truncated semantics are one parameter

dilation keeps the reference per-offset formula (splat loop over offsets with cov > 0) so the result is bit-identical; cost grows with (2 * ceil(grown_px) + 1)^2 per output sample, so very large spread values are refused by max_work instead of approximated
WindowError is a new non_exhaustive type; EffectError is not extended
not_addressed: no cancellation or deadline hook inside a window (cost is bounded by max_work only)
dilation is O(window area * offsets); a distance-transform fast path would have to be bit-identical to the reference ramp, which it is not for non-binary alpha, so it was not attempted
the accessor is called per row; a band-wise accessor is an additive follow-up if a consumer needs it
render-cpu still refuses margins above 24 px until it adopts this API (consumer change, not in this crate)
